text: The document shall be converted into an OCR-searchable PDF or PDF/A.
why: A flat scan with no text layer cannot be searched, indexed or read by the Registry's systems. This is the single most common technical rejection in e-filing, and it is invisible to the eye — the PDF looks perfectly fine on screen.
source: E-filing Rules of the High Court of Delhi, 2021

fix.guidance: Re-export the document as an OCR-searchable PDF or PDF/A. Most PDF tools do this under 'Recognise text' / 'Make searchable'.

text: The maximum file size for e-filing is 100 MB in the High Court (20 MB in the District Courts).
why: An oversized bundle is rejected by the portal itself, before a human ever sees it. Advocates have re-filed the same appeal repeatedly against this cap.
source: E-filing Rules of the High Court of Delhi, 2021

fix.guidance: Downsample image-only pages and re-export. PARAM can compress the bundle under the cap without touching text pages.

text: PDF files are to be book-marked as provided in the rules.
why: Bookmarks are how the bench navigates an electronic paperbook. A long bundle with no bookmark tree is hard to use even when it is otherwise in order.
source: E-filing Rules of the High Court of Delhi, 2021

fix.guidance: Add a bookmark per document and per annexure. PARAM can build the tree from the classified bundle.

text: Blank pages should not form part of the e-filed paperbook.
why: Blank pages inflate the pagination and desynchronise the index from the actual bundle, which then reads as a pagination defect.
source: E-filing Rules of the High Court of Delhi, 2021 (scrutiny practice)

fix.guidance: Remove blank pages and repaginate. PARAM can do both together.
